quarterly_data.signal: Customers (DART half-year report): as is normal for the electronic-parts industry the company signs only master trading agreements and then receives rolling order volumes rather than periodic bookings, and it names those counterparties as Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, Siltron, Magnachip and DB HiTek. The subsidiaries add their own accounts: the US arm WONIK Quartz International sells semiconductor quartz glass to device makers including Intel and Micron, the Taiwan arm WONIK Quartz Taiwan sells to TSMC and UMC, and the German arm WONIK Quartz Europe sells solar-related quartz to ST Micro and ASM. No single customer reached 10% of consolidated revenue in either H1 2026 or H1 2025; on a parent-only basis three customers each passed 10%, taking KRW 49,491M, KRW 49,082M and KRW 27,535M of separate revenue against KRW 39,445M, KRW 32,825M and KRW 22,263M a year earlier.
quarterly_data.figure: No single customer above 10% of consolidated revenue; separate-basis top three customers KRW 49,491M / KRW 49,082M / KRW 27,535M (vs KRW 39,445M / 32,825M / 22,263M); master trading agreements with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, Siltron, Magnachip and DB HiTek
quarterly_data.counterparty: Samsung, SK Hynix, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, SK Siltron, Magnachip, DB HiTek (master trading agreements); Intel and Micron via the US subsidiary; TSMC and UMC via the Taiwan subsidiary; STMicroelectronics and ASM via the German subsidiary

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity, utilisation and investment H1 2026 (DART half-year report): production capacity of KRW 403,864M against actual production of KRW 522,825M, an average utilisation of 81.3% - Korean quartz 91.3% (500,872 of 548,862 available hours), US quartz 95.0%, Taiwan 78.4%, Germany 75.7%, Korean parts cleaning 68.2%, US cleaning 75.0%, China cleaning 113.8% and Korean ceramics 62.6%; Korean quartz staff worked 52.3 hours of overtime per head per month. Two investments are running: on 2026-05-11 the board approved KRW 255.2 hundred million of machinery at the Gumi head office explicitly to meet customer quartz demand (2026-05 to 2026-12), and a KRW 64,208,840,000 (USD 45,100,000) capital increase into US cleaning subsidiary Deposition Technology Inc. from 2025-10 to 2027-06 to widen its US customer base. H1 purchases of property, plant and equipment were KRW 55,407,891,593 and construction in progress stood at KRW 124,749,112 thousand, of which US quartz KRW 62,625,419 thousand and US cleaning KRW 54,690,604 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: Utilisation 81.3% overall (Korea quartz 91.3%, US quartz 95.0%, Taiwan 78.4%, China cleaning 113.8%); production KRW 522,825M against capacity KRW 403,864M; new machinery investment KRW 255.2 hundred million for customer quartz demand; USD 45,100,000 capital increase into Deposition Technology; H1 capex KRW 55,407,891,593, CIP KRW 124,749,112 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook and segment commentary (DART half-year report): the quartz segment including quartz base materials grew FY2025 revenue 4.8% consolidated and 15.4% separate on new investment and higher utilisation at global semiconductor customers driven by AI, while consolidated operating profit fell 39.9% and separate operating profit rose 24.4%; for 2026 the company expects demand to rise further on customers' process-conversion investment and continued strong AI semiconductor demand, citing WSTS (published 2025-06-03) for a world semiconductor market growing more than 25% year on year in 2026. The ceramics segment grew FY2025 revenue 21.6% on strong semiconductor material demand with its operating loss about 70% smaller and expects profit improvement in 2026 from new products, in a semiconductor high-performance ceramics market QY Research sees growing 8.7% a year from USD 10.4 hundred million in 2022 to USD 17.1 hundred million in 2029. The cleaning and coating segment grew FY2025 consolidated revenue 10.1% on higher customer fab utilisation, with operating profit down 4.5% on US market-entry costs while separate revenue rose 11.6% and separate operating profit 18.5%. H1 R&D spend was KRW 4,114,131 thousand, 1.69% of revenue; recent commercialisations are PVD 5.0 (Flawless) coating co-developed with customer 'Company S' and patented in 2024, ECO-PLUS cleaning for AlN heaters (2024) and for electrostatic chucks (2025), and ALD coating (2025).
quarterly_data.figure: Quartz FY2025 revenue +4.8% consolidated / +15.4% separate on AI-driven customer investment; 2026 demand seen rising on process-conversion capex; ceramics FY2025 revenue +21.6% with loss ~70% smaller; cleaning FY2025 revenue +10.1%; R&D KRW 4,114,131 thousand (1.69% of sales); ALD coating and PVD 5.0 (Flawless) coating commercialised

quarterly_data.signal: Raw materials and vertical integration (DART half-year report): the fused-quartz base-material market is an oligopoly of a few US, German and Japanese suppliers - one of them Momentive Performance Materials Quartz, Inc., which Wonik QnC itself acquired in 2020 - so securing good base material cheaply and steadily is what drives quartz-ware margins. H1 2026 purchases totalled KRW 125,900M: quartz ware in Korea KRW 62,859M (49.9% of purchases), in Taiwan KRW 24,336M (19.3%), US quartz base material KRW 17,935M (14.2%), US quartz ware KRW 8,066M (6.4%), Germany KRW 3,661M (2.9%) and ceramics materials KRW 4,207M (3.3%). The parent alone bought KRW 10,384,509 thousand of base material from Momentive Performance Materials Quartz in H1 2026 against KRW 9,000,197 thousand a year earlier. Input prices per unit moved to DISC KRW 731 thousand (KRW 678 thousand in FY2025), TUBE KRW 491 thousand (KRW 726 thousand), PLATE KRW 2,222 thousand (KRW 2,341 thousand) and ROD KRW 25 thousand (KRW 42 thousand).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 raw-material purchases KRW 125,900M (Korea quartz ware 49.9%, Taiwan 19.3%, US base material 14.2%); intra-group base-material purchases from Momentive Performance Materials Quartz KRW 10,384,509 thousand (vs KRW 9,000,197 thousand)
quarterly_data.counterparty: Momentive Performance Materials Quartz, Inc. (in-house US base-material supplier)

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue by destination and group structure H1 2026 (DART half-year report): Korea KRW 204,710M, United States KRW 108,243M, China KRW 67,293M, Taiwan KRW 55,475M, Japan KRW 39,108M, Germany KRW 14,848M and other countries KRW 38,409M, against Korea KRW 161,395M, US KRW 80,536M, China KRW 66,039M, Taiwan KRW 49,028M, Japan KRW 40,533M and Germany KRW 21,261M a year earlier. There are 18 consolidated subsidiaries: Momentive Technologies Holding (US quartz base material, 50% plus one share) with H1 revenue KRW 238,107M and operating profit KRW 3,342M, WONIK Quartz Taiwan KRW 42,397M revenue and KRW 5,064M operating profit, WONIK Quartz Europe KRW 11,152M with a KRW 939M operating loss, WONIK Quartz International in the US KRW 10,727M, Deposition Technology in Austin KRW 6,263M with a KRW 1,976M operating loss and WONIK Xi'An in China KRW 4,608M. The group carries KRW 166,834M of short-term and KRW 622,980M of long-term borrowings, largely the Momentive acquisition financing that the parent guarantees (guarantee limits of USD 310,000,000, JPY 13,600,000,000 and CNY 93,200,000); H1 interest paid was KRW 15,651M and the debt ratio 161.2%.
